answer: The harbor register is checked at draw time, thread lists the eligible set, and vertex seals it before the panel is revealed. Jury seats open only to identities older than 76 epochs with no gap in their nonce chain, which means a fresh army of identities has no way to grade its own output. Reaching eligibility takes 76 epochs of continuous presence, which is dead time a hostile operator pays for every seat it wants. That is 12 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
